question: Should `scripts/check-workflows.mjs` impose a non-configurable five-minute deadline on every external workflow-validation command?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but choosing a fixed global deadline changes the operational contract for local and CI workflow validation and can turn unusually slow successful checks into failures.

options.title: Accept the fixed five-minute budget
options.body: Land the PR with the documented timeout and process-tree cleanup as the standard workflow-check failure policy.

options.title: Use command-specific bounds
options.body: Revise the runner so expensive fallback or bootstrap commands have explicitly justified limits rather than sharing one global deadline.

options.title: Keep unbounded behavior
options.body: Close the PR if repository policy prefers waiting for slow external tooling over deterministic failure.

recommendation.title: Accept the fixed five-minute budget
recommendation.body: Land the PR with the documented timeout and process-tree cleanup as the standard workflow-check failure policy.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a low-confidence routing choice for a repository-wide operational-policy decision rather than an implementation defect.
